assets.media_asset.description: Required before use in a guest-facing surface. WCAG 2.2 AA.
Signed and expiring for private assets; stable CDN URL for public ones.
How many surfaces reference this asset. Non-zero refuses deletion.

assets.media_usage.description: True where the referencing surface is published to guests.

assets.media_upload.description: Signed. PUT the file here, then confirm with `/complete`.

fnb.delivery_location.description: What a runner is told. "Cabana 12", "Row H Seat 4", "Lawn — north gate".
Set where the location is a restaurant table, so it shares table state.
Set where the seat is the address. References the seat map.
Which outlets deliver here. A cabana served by the pool bar and not the restaurant is normal, and a location nothing serves is not an address.
False where the location exists but is not currently taking delivery — closed section, weather, no runner on shift.
From the serving outlet. Feeds the guest's estimate — a cabana eight minutes away is not the same promise as a table by the kitchen.

fnb.location_session.description: The outlet serving this location. Where several serve it, the guest chooses and this is set on the first order.
The table visit this session orders onto, where the location is a table. Absent for a cabana or a seat, which have no visit concept — the order stands alone.
Sessions expire so a guest who leaves cannot order to a lounger now occupied by someone else.

fnb.table_session.description: The table visit this session orders onto. An existing open visit is joined rather than duplicated — a guest seated by a server and then ordering by app is one party, one
Sessions expire so a guest who leaves cannot order to a table now occupied by someone else.

fnb.menu_item.description: The catalogue variant this item sells. Pricing and tax come from there — a menu is a presentation of the catalogue, not a second catalogue.
True where a recipe exists. Stock-tracked items cannot be sold offline.

fnb.modifier_group.description: Greater than zero makes the group required.

fnb.kitchen_ticket.description: Higher fires sooner. Raised by Fast Pass or supervisor override.

fnb.kitchen_station.description: Where the venue's KDS listens. Absent where a fallback screen is used instead.

games.card.description: From a promotion. Typically non-refundable and spent before paid credits.
Won by playing. Buys prizes. **Not interchangeable with credits** — a guest who wins should not simply be able to play more.

games.game.description: The machine. Taken out of service by maintenance, the game stops accepting play rather than swallowing credits.

games.prize.description: Links to retail. Redemption depletes stock through the inventory ledger — a prize wall running out is a stock problem and should look like one.
Small, medium, large, jackpot. Drives prize-wall layout.

games.redemption.description: Movements raised in the inventory ledger.

inventory.item.description: The unit stock is held in. Immutable once movements exist.
How the supplier sells it — a case of 24 against a base unit of one.
True permits issue beyond on-hand. Occasionally needed at a bar mid-service; dangerous everywhere else.
Derived from movements. Not directly editable.
True locks costing method and base unit.

inventory.movement.description: Positive increases stock, negative decreases it.
Required for adjustments, which are reported separately.
What generated it — an order, a count, a transfer.

inventory.goods_receipt.description: The accrual the supplier invoice will later match against.

maintenance.asset.description: Products this asset delivers. A fault here can stop them selling.
Access point this asset controls. Out of service blocks it.
True means a completed inspection is required before return to service. A technician cannot simply declare a ride safe.
Cycles, hours or kilometres. Drives usage-based maintenance.

maintenance.maintenance_plan.description: Applies to every asset in the category rather than one.
Usage trigger — cycles, hours, kilometres. **Whichever comes first** when both are set. A ride serviced every three months or ten thousand cycles is one plan.
How far ahead the work order is generated, so parts can be ordered before the job is already late.

maintenance.inspection_template.description: Compliance inspections are retained alongside the financial trail.

maintenance.inspection_template_item.description: A failed safety-critical item **blocks the inspection from passing** and cannot be overridden by completing the rest.

maintenance.inspection.description: An inspection nobody signed is not an inspection.

maintenance.incident.description: Requires notification to an external authority within a statutory window.

marketing.guest_profile.description: Opaque reference. Personal data lives in the separately erasable store, which is what makes erasure possible against an append-only ledger.
Present where the guest is linked across cells. Marketing acts locally.

marketing.guest_device.description: Hash of the token, not the token. The token itself is write-only — returning it would put a push credential in every response a support agent can read.
Consecutive delivery failures. Past the threshold the device is marked failed and stops being targeted — a dead token retried forever is wasted quota and a misleading del

marketing.consent_purpose.description: Current version of the notice. A consent against a superseded version is reported as requiring renewal rather than silently honoured.
True for transactional. Withdrawing it means the service cannot be delivered, so it is presented differently.

marketing.consent_record.description: Omit to apply to every channel the purpose covers.

marketing.segment_criterion.description: Behavioural or profile attribute — visit count, last visit, lifetime value, product purchased, membership tier, venue visited, language.

marketing.campaign.description: Hours during which sending is permitted. A promotional message at 3am is a complaint waiting to happen.

marketing.message_template.description: Per language, keyed by ISO 639-1 code.
Required for WhatsApp, where templates are pre-approved by the provider.

marketing.case.description: Accrued only while awaiting the guest. Waiting on an internal team does not pause the clock.

marketing.loyalty_programme.description: Points post here on accrual. They are a liability from the moment they are earned, not from the moment they are spent.

marketing.review.description: Aspect chips — exhibitions, staff, cleanliness, food, value.
Case raised automatically where the rating fell below the venue's threshold. Feedback that goes nowhere is worse than no feedback mechanism.

control.migration.description: A rollback section exists and CI has executed it against a restored snapshot. A rollback nobody has run is a comment, not a rollback.
Compared on apply. A migration edited after it was applied somewhere is a defect the register catches, not a mystery to debug later.

control.migration_plan.description: A plan is computed against cell state at a moment. Beyond this it is stale and apply refuses it rather than applying to a different world than it was made for.

control.migration_plan_cell.description: A long lock on a partitioned table during trading hours is the output this endpoint exists to produce.

control.environment.description: How long a release must sit here before it may be promoted. Zero for dev; a real number for staging, or staging is a formality.

control.upgrade_schedule.description: Beyond this the platform proceeds. An indefinitely deferred tenant becomes a version nobody supports.

promotions.promotion.description: Higher evaluates first where several could apply.
Total discount value after which the promotion stops automatically.

promotions.coupon_campaign.description: True generates individually redeemable codes. False issues one shared code with a redemption limit.

promotions.coupon_code.description: Why the code cannot be applied. A cashier reading `expired` to a guest is a very different conversation from reading `already used`.

promotions.voucher_batch.description: False forfeits any unused balance, which is then recognised as breakage.
Unredeemed value. A liability until redeemed or expired.

promotions.bundle_component.description: For dynamic bundles — guest chooses among these.
Where this component is redeemed. Differs from the selling venue for multi-venue passes, which is why the allocation split exists.

promotions.allocation_component.description: For `proRataListPrice` — weights derived from list prices.
Set where the component is earned by a different legal entity. Cross-currency allocation is deferred pending the FX policy decision.

promotions.allocation_split.description: True where components are earned by different legal entities. Such splits generate inter-company positions.

promotions.bundle.description: Sum of component list prices less the bundle price.
True locks components and allocation against amendment.

promotions.upsell_rule.description: Empty applies to every channel. Restriction is opt-in — a rule that fires on the website but not at a counter is a guest experience inconsistency.

queue.queue.description: The ride. Taking it out of service closes this queue rather than leaving guests holding positions for something that is not running.
How long a called party has to arrive before the entry expires.
Share of each cycle reserved for Fast Pass holders.

queue.entry.description: What the guest sees and what appears on signage.

queue.feed.description: Key vault reference. Credentials are never returned.
Beyond this without a reading, the feed is considered quiet.

queue.reading.description: Deliberately narrow. Anything richer would couple the platform to one vendor's model of a queue.

reporting.report_filter.description: Prompted at run time rather than fixed. Parameters narrow the result; they never widen scope.

reporting.report_definition.description: Permission needed to run this report. **The author cannot assign one they do not hold** — otherwise a venue user could build themselves a tenant-wide view.
Guards against a query spanning years of scan events.
Shipped with the platform. Cannot be amended, only cloned.
Informs whether it may run inline or must be queued.

reporting.execution.description: The version this ran against. With the parameters and scope below, it is everything needed to reproduce the result.
Scope paths the caller held. What constrained the result.
Results are retained for a limited period, then discarded.

reporting.schedule.description: An empty report every morning trains people to ignore the report.
The schedule runs under this principal's permissions, not the recipients'. A standing grant of whatever the owner can see.

reporting.export.description: Signed and expiring. Present only while status is `ready`.

reporting.dashboard_tile.description: Minimum thirty seconds. A tile refreshing every second is a load problem wearing a convenience costume.

reporting.dashboard.description: Combined refresh load of every tile.

retail.merchandise.description: The catalogue variant sold. Price and tax come from there.
The stock item depleted on sale. Null means the item sells but never runs out, which is almost always a configuration error.

retail.sale.description: The order in the Order & Payment context. Retail does not keep its own ledger.

retail.sale_line.description: False once the window has passed or the line is fully returned.

retail.return.description: The refund raised in the Order & Payment context.

retail.return_line.description: False for opened, damaged or faulty goods, which are written off with a reason rather than silently absent.

retail.return_policy.description: Up to this, one cashier may accept a return alone.
Conditions that return stock to sale. Everything else is written off.

retail.exchange.description: Positive means the guest pays; negative means a refund is due. Only the difference settles.

retail.wallet.description: Promotional value. Typically non-refundable and spent first.
Where the authoritative balance lives. Present when the guest is linked across cells.

retail.shop_and_drop.description: Short and readable. Printed on the slip a guest may or may not keep.
The ticket that claims these goods. The point of 4.4.7 — a guest does not have to keep a receipt safe for eight hours in a water park.

seating.seat_map.description: False when only a manifest has been imported. Such a map can be sold from a list but not rendered.

seating.section.description: Polygon for rendering. Absent without geometry.

seating.section_row.description: Which end row numbering starts from. Not recoverable from a manifest and must be stated — it determines whether a guest finds their seat.

seating.seat.description: **Stable for the life of the seat.** Section, row and number are display labels that change on a refit; this does not. A ticket sold today must still resolve after a renu
Present on accessible seats. Sold together, released together.

seating.seat_category.description: Ordering for best-seat assignment. Lower is better.

seating.import_job.description: Geometry imports — seats successfully joined to the manifest.
Present in one source but not the other. A seat in the plan with no manifest entry is a finding, not a seat.

seating.seat_hold.description: Neighbours implicitly held by a seating rule.

seating.seating_rules.description: Seats kept empty either side of a sold party.
Refuse a selection that would leave a single unsellable seat between parties. Operators want this and rarely ask for it by name.
A party must sit together or the selection is refused.
Companion seats sold alongside each accessible space.

control.plan.description: Branded native publishing carries per-tenant operational cost and is priced, not absorbed.
Existing subscribers stay on the version they were sold. A price change never applies retroactively.

control.usage_record.description: For AI token usage — which capability consumed them.

control.invoice.description: Priced against the version the tenant is subscribed to, not the latest.

whitelabel.navigation_item.description: At most five may be visible in bottom navigation; the rest overflow.

whitelabel.promo_block.description: Presentation only. A block may point at a promotion; it does not create or price one.

whitelabel.policy.description: Immutable. A guest who consented to version 3 consented to version 3, and a policy that changes under a recorded consent is a compliance failure.

whitelabel.module_enablement.description: From the tenant's subscription. False makes enablement impossible.

whitelabel.feature_toggle.description: True where the feature needs credentials or setup elsewhere first.

whitelabel.config_version.description: Changes in this version that will not reach guests until the next store release. Surfaced at publish so nobody expects a new icon tomorrow.

access.admission_profile.description: How long before a performance validation opens.
Empty means any access point in the venue.

access.scan_event.description: Null while pending. Differs from recordedAt for offline scans.

catalogue.entitlement_template.description: Null means unlimited. The Fast Pass consumption counter lives here.
Whether this entitlement may be scanned to claim goods left under 4.4.7. False for a single-entry ticket that is surrendered at the gate — a claim token the guest no long
True requires a holder name at sale. Most entitlements carry none — identity and entitlement are separate concerns.
True propagates a redemption right to other cells on issue (ADR-0010).

catalogue.product.description: True only when live **and** carried by a published bundle. Approval and publication are different acts.
What the buyer receives. Null for products that grant nothing — F&B and retail. Identity and entitlement are separate concerns.
True for seated and retail. Seated because a seat map is not a count; retail because stock depletes in real time.
Custom fields. JSONB-backed, defined by the venue's data mask.

catalogue.variant.description: False when retired. Retired variants are never deleted — orders reference them.

catalogue.price_list.description: Where lists overlap, higher priority wins.

catalogue.envelope.description: True where capacity is divided across channels. Leases then draw from a channel allocation rather than from raw capacity.
Seated envelopes cannot be leased and are blocked offline. A seat map is not a count.

catalogue.channel_allocation.description: Unsold units return to the general pool at this time. How distribution holds are freed close to a performance without someone remembering to do it.

catalogue.published_bundle.description: Present when `isDelta`. The version this delta applies to.
Detached signature over `contentHash`. The terminal verifies before applying and rolls back on failure — a half-applied catalogue is never traded against.
Products, variants, price lists, prices, tax codes, events, performances, envelope definitions and data mask field definitions. Shape is versioned with the bundle format,

catalogue.inventory_lease.description: Present when sub-leased from a venue edge node.
May be less than requested — a partial grant is not an error. Constrained by the channel's remaining allocation plus the general pool, never by raw capacity.

platform.guest_link.description: Pseudonymous. Not derived from any personal data. This is the only identifier that crosses a cell boundary.
Cell of first registration. Authoritative for the wallet balance.
Version of the consent notice shown when the link was created. Retained as the transfer basis.

platform.redemption_right.description: Null where the right is valid at any venue in the consuming cell.

ledger.account.description: Code in the client's own chart. Used on export so their team sees their codes.
False for parent accounts, which aggregate only.

ledger.account_mapping.description: Null applies the mapping to every venue in the region.

ledger.tax_code.description: When set, this tax applies to the base **plus** the referenced tax, not to the base alone. Ordering is explicit rather than implied.
True when the displayed price already contains this tax.

ledger.tax_exemption.description: Identifier of the exempt subject, matching `scope`.

ledger.recognition_schedule.description: Days after expiry at which unredeemed value becomes breakage.

ledger.journal_entry.description: The order, refund or run that generated this entry.

ledger.price_variance.description: The bundle the terminal priced from. Turns "the price was wrong" into "the terminal was two bundles behind", which is actionable.
Above the venue's configured variance threshold.

identity.sso_provider.description: True disables password login for principals covered by this provider.

identity.sso_group_mapping.description: Scope the mapped role is granted at.

identity.mfa_method.description: Partially masked destination, so a person can tell two methods apart.

identity.principal.description: Past this, resolution returns DENY regardless of grants.
Determines the landing screen when the principal holds several roles and picks one at login.

identity.grant.description: From the permission enum. `*` permitted on DENY only.

orders.ticket_transfer.description: Set only on claim. Ownership moves then, not at offer.
An unclaimed transfer expires and the tickets return. A transfer to a mistyped address must not strand a ticket somewhere nobody can reach.

orders.order_line.description: Lease the units were drawn from. Absent for uncontended products.
Seated products only. Not available offline.
What the client charged, from its local bundle.
What the server computed on ingest.
Server minus quoted. Non-zero means the quoted price was honoured and the difference posted to the variance account.
Redemption rights propagated to other cells for this line.

orders.sales_order.description: Sum across lines. Zero on a normal order.

orders.refund_policy.description: Up to this, a holder of ORDER_REFUND refunds alone. Zero means every refund needs a second authoriser.
Above this, a second user — cashier OR supervisor — names themselves as audit control. Dual-authorisation, not escalation (2.12.3).
Above this, an ORDER_REFUND_APPROVE holder must approve.
Refundable percentage by time before the performance. Evaluated most-specific first.
Price variance above this is an exception requiring review rather than a routine posting (CF-38). Venue-configured.

orders.refund.description: From the venue's time bands, or an approver override.
Written before the gateway is called.

orders.shift.description: Client-generated ULID. Also the idempotency key.
Who opened it. Cash reconciles to a person and a drawer.
Inventory leases currently held by this workstation. Surfaced so an operator closing a shift can see what will be returned.
When the device recorded the open. Differs from `openedAt` when offline.
Null while the shift has unsynced operations.

orders.cash_movement.description: Safe drop reference or bag number.
The principal who authorised the movement, recorded for audit.
Monotonic within the shift. Preserves order across an offline batch.

platform.outlet.description: Where this outlet draws stock from. A shop and its stockroom are one location; a bar drawing from a central cellar is not.
Revenue and cost attribution. Outlet is the natural grain for both.

platform.device.description: Built to an open standard where one exists — ESC/POS, UnifiedPOS, OSDP. Adding a vendor is a driver plus configuration, not a core change (ADR-0015).
True blocks shift open when the device is unreachable.

platform.scope_node.description: False causes every permission query at or beneath this node to resolve to DENY.

platform.region_settings.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. Determines the jurisdiction, and therefore the cell.
Decimal places for this region's currency. Varies by currency — some use 2, some use 3. Money columns are numeric(18,4) and carry the scale explicitly, because a fixed 2-

platform.workstation.description: Determines which front end loads. Bound to the workstation, not the role — the F&B terminal opens the F&B board. What the operator may then DO within it is governed by th
Inherited from the workstation, never selected by the operator. Null where the workstation is not at an access point.
Derived from `deploymentProfile`. False only for `thin`. Under local-first, catalogue READS are always local on transactional surfaces; this flag governs whether WRITES c

marketing.wishlist_item.description: Owner. Keyed by subject; there is no parent wishlist row.
False where the product has been withdrawn or the performance has passed. Returned rather than dropped — a guest who saved something and finds it silently gone assumes th

pii.subject.description: What to call this person. Forcing every name into given plus family is a Western assumption that fails visibly in the Gulf
An erased subject keeps its row as a tombstone. Deleting it would break every foreign key and cascade into removing sales from the ledger

pii.subject_contact.description: email, mobile, phone, whatsapp or postal
Lowercased email, E.164 mobile. Matching on the raw value means the same person registers twice with two capitalisations
Deterministic hash. Finds a guest by email without the search path reading plaintext, and checks a suppression list without holding the address it suppresses
Set only by a completed verification. This is what makes guest checkout linking safe — orders attach on a verified identifier, never a claim

pii.subject_document.description: passport, emiratesId, nationalId, drivingLicence, residencePermit, other
**Hashed.** A full passport number in a queryable column is the single worst row in any venue database, and no operation needs it
In clear, for a human to confirm against the card in front of them
A scan where one was taken. Object storage with its own retention — an image of a passport in a database backup travels further than anyone intends

pii.subject_biometric.description: Reference into the biometric store. **Never the template, never the image it came from**
**A foreign key, not a boolean.** The specific consent authorising enrolment can be produced on demand (CF-35)
Enrolment expires. An indefinite biometric enrolment is one nobody re-consented to

qdrant:knowledge.description: The embedding. **Dimension is fixed by the collection** — a shard cannot differ (ADR-0021)
**The shard key, and the tenant boundary on shared placement.** Set at provisioning, never from a request
**Filtered on every query, from the resolved session.** Indexed — Qdrant filters before the vector search, not after
Which of the eleven RAG sources this chunk came from
The row it was derived from. **Erasure and re-index both key on this**
Set where chunkStrategy is parentChild — retrieve the child, return the parent
Indexed. Lets a query narrow to policies, menu items or cases without a second collection
The language the chunk is written in
Staleness. **Non-zero drift against the source is the number `staleCount` reports**

cache:answer.description: **question hash + scope_path + locale.** Scope is part of the key — a cache keyed on the question alone is a cross-venue leak
The response and its cited sources
`AiPolicy.cacheTtlMinutes`. An upper bound on top of event invalidation, not instead of it
Which event dropped it, kept for a period so a stale answer can be traced

cache:embedding.description: **content hash + model.** The key changes when the content does, which is why invalidation is trivial
**Part of the key.** A vector from another model is not comparable and must not be served

cache:resolution.description: scope_path + what is being resolved — permissions, configuration, a price list
Bumped by the write that evicts it. **A config change nobody evicts is a stale permission**

cache:idempotency.description: The idempotency key the caller sent
**Scoped to the caller** — two tills may legitimately generate the same key
Replayed verbatim, so a retry returns what the first call returned
**Must exceed the longest offline window.** A scanner out for a weekend replays on Monday

nomap: projection over outlet, menu and table state
projection over menu, item and availability
union view over work orders, inspections and incidents
wrapper. The items are the table, keyed by subject
result set, cached in object storage
computed from seat, hold and block
computed from order, payment, refund and ledger

storage.platform.schema_version: Migration bookkeeping. **Written by the migrator, never by an operation**
storage.platform.outbox: **Written in the same transaction as the state change, by the platform, not by an operation.** That is what makes it exactly-once
storage.platform.tenant: read-only projection of control.tenant, outside every cell
storage.platform.sale_board_tile: Child of sale_board_page, which is a child of sale_board. **Two levels down, returned nested**
storage.identity.principal_credential: a credential hash has no response it belongs in
storage.identity.authz_audit: **Written by the authorisation layer on every call**, not by an operation
storage.orders.sales_order_unassigned: Default partition. **No operation names it**; the partition router does
storage.access.scan_event_unassigned: Default partition — rows land here before a scope resolves. **No operation names it**; the partition router does
storage.fnb.delivery_location_outlet: join table. Which outlets serve which locations
storage.fnb.location_code: Rotating, hashed, time-bounded. **Generated by a job, resolved at claim** — never directly created or listed
storage.orders.no_sale_event: drawer opened without a sale. Recorded because it is the classic cover for theft
storage.orders.order_discount: manual discount with reason and approver. Posts to a discount account, never as a price change
storage.orders.payment_tip: tips post to a liability, not to sales
storage.orders.order_media_link: links an order to the media its entitlements were issued onto. What makes append-to-existing possible without editing a paid order
storage.ledger.fx_rate: configured rates with effective windows. A rate change is a new row; the old is never edited
storage.ledger.inter_entity_obligation: what one legal entity owes another after a cross-region redemption
storage.control.cell_cluster: identical cells serving a region. Scaling out is launching another, not growing one
storage.control.tenant_migration: a tenant moving between cells — shared to dedicated, or rebalancing
storage.control.tenant_migration_plan: computed against cell state; expires, because a plan made for a different world is not a plan
storage.ai.provider: Configured providers, models and failover order. Credentials are a vault reference, never a key
storage.ai.policy: What the assistant may do, which roles may use it, what is masked. Resolves tenant then venue (ADR-0018)
storage.ai.conversation: A thread, scoped to a principal and a module. **Analytical store, not the transactional primary** (ADR-0020) — append-only with an analytical read pattern, and it must not compete with a gate scan for a connection.
storage.ai.message: Prompt and response with sources, provider, model, tokens and latency. **Analytical store, not the transactional primary** (ADR-0020) — append-only with an analytical read pattern, and it must not compete with a gate scan for a connection.
storage.ai.interaction: The audit record. **Retention is unresolved (CF-64)** — a prompt may carry personal data. **Analytical store, not the transactional primary** (ADR-0020) — append-only with an analytical read pattern, and it must not compete with a gate scan for a connection.
storage.ai.proposed_action: A draft the assistant produced and a person must approve. Nothing executes from here
storage.ai.knowledge_collection: A collection in the vector store. **One per embedding model** — a collection carries its own vector config and a shard cannot, so two models cannot share one (ADR-0021). Carries the shard key, which is the tenant boundary on shared placement
storage.ai.knowledge_document: Source, status and chunk count. The text and its vectors live in Qdrant
storage.ai.chunk_ref: Maps a Qdrant point id back to its document and scope. **The join between the two stores**
storage.ai.index_source: One declaration per indexed table. The owning service does not know it exists — the AI service consumes the event that service already publishes
storage.ai.index_job: A build in flight. recordsFailed is the number to watch — a source failing on 3% of rows is a search missing 3% of answers
storage.ai.index_entry: Maps a source row to its Qdrant point ids, so a deletion in Postgres can be followed into the vector store. **Nothing cascades between the two**
storage.approvals.request: One request per action needing authorisation. The subject is a reference, never a copy
storage.approvals.decision: Every decision at every level. **Immutable once the request completes** — an approval is evidence
storage.approvals.matrix: What requires approval where. Versioned, because a request must be decided by the rules it was raised under
storage.approvals.rule: Ordered within a matrix. First match wins, so adding a rule cannot silently change another
storage.approvals.delegation: Standing in for an approver. Always time-bounded — an open-ended delegation is one nobody remembers
storage.approvals.escalation: Who was asked, when, and why it moved up. The original approver stays in the record
storage.orders.credit_override: a manual override of a partner credit limit, recorded with who and why. Second table on a marker the deriver only read the first half of
storage.control.release: a shipped version. Promoted through dev, staging and production; superseded by a later one
storage.games.credit_ledger: credits bought, played and won. The arcade equivalent of a wallet
storage.identity.session: a staff session, carrying the workstation and the selected role
storage.identity.guest_session: a guest session. Separate from staff — different lifetime, different auth
storage.identity.mfa_challenge: an issued MFA challenge and its outcome
storage.identity.otp_challenge: a one-time code sent to a guest contact point
storage.inventory.stock_level: quantity on hand per item per location. **Gates the sale at outlet level** (14 August)
storage.marketing.message_delivery: one row per recipient per send. Delivery, bounce and engagement
storage.orders.cash_count_line: a denomination and a count from a blind till count
storage.reporting.report_field: the fields a report definition may use. Retrievable, so a report can be found by what it answers
storage.workforce.rota_assignment: A person expected somewhere at a time. **Not a shift** — a shift is a cash session, and most people on a rota never touch a till
storage.workforce.shift_swap: Both parties agree before the supervisor sees it. Routed through approvals rather than a second mechanism
storage.workforce.attendance: Who actually turned up. **occurredAt and recordedAt are both kept** — a steward clocking in offline is not late because the sync was
storage.workforce.announcement: Targeted by venue, department or role. `emergency` is not a louder `operational`
storage.workforce.announcement_receipt: Delivered and acknowledged, per principal. **The outstanding list is the roll call**
storage.maintenance.work_order_attachment: Photo, video, document, note or signature against a work order. Evidence, not decoration — captured offline and queued
storage.promotions.bundle_choice_group: Pick n from a set. The bundle price does not move with the choice (ADR-0019) — the allocation does
storage.platform.audit_record: **Written by the platform on every write, not by any one operation** (ADR-0022 sits above this). Naming it on 431 lineage rows would say nothing
storage.platform.audit_read: **PII reads only**, written by the platform. Who looked at a passport number is the question a regulator asks
storage.orders.cart: A cart holds leases; an order holds money. Retained after expiry so a recovery link lands on something
storage.orders.cart_line: One line, with the lease that holds its capacity. Null lease for a product with no capacity
storage.catalogue.donation_campaign: Fixed, free or round-up. **Posts to a liability account, not revenue** — money collected for a charity is not the venue’s to recognise
storage.catalogue.waitlist_entry: Who asked to be told when a sold-out session frees up. **Not a queue** — a queue is people standing at a ride
storage.fnb.table_reservation: A booking with a time and a party size. Distinct from a table session, which is a guest already sitting down
storage.orders.donation_line: A donation within a transaction. A line, not a flag, because one transaction may give to several campaigns
storage.control.partner_agreement: Net rate or commission, credit terms, validity. **Versioned** — an order placed last week used last week’s rate
storage.access.parking_facility: A car park and its integration mode. Three modes, and the mode decides what happens at sale (CF-52)
storage.access.parking_entitlement: A guest bought parking. Carries the plate where the mode is plateWhitelist — **personal data**, since a plate identifies a person
storage.ai.layout_draft: A generated seat layout awaiting review. **Ends at previewReady and writes nothing to the seat map** — the draft enters seating.import_job at its existing human commit step (ADR-0020)
storage.qdrant:knowledge: **One collection per embedding model** (ADR-0021) — a collection is the only Qdrant container that can carry its own vector configuration, and a shard cannot. Tenants sharing a model share this collection, separated by shard key and scope_path payload; a tenant forced onto a local model by residency gets its own
storage.orders.deposit_box: A cashier’s cash box. **Allocated to a person, not a workstation** — a cashier moving between tills takes their float, which is what makes a variance attributable. withdrawnTotal reduces the expected close: cash skimmed for banking is not a shortfall
storage.marketing.conversation: A live session with somebody waiting. **Not a case** — a case is a ticket measured in hours, this is measured in seconds. A conversation may create a case; it is not one
storage.marketing.conversation_message: One message. The sender is resolved, never declared, and **the assistant is labelled as one** — a guest talking to a bot that presents as a person is a complaint waiting to happen
storage.marketing.kiosk_assist_session: A staff member acting on a kiosk session remotely (2.1.25). **The guest can always see it and always end it** — assistance a guest cannot stop is surveillance
storage.marketing.agent_availability: Available, busy, away or offline, with a concurrency limit. **Expires** — an agent who forgets to go offline is one conversations queue for
storage.cache:answer: **Question, scope and locale to an answer.** The largest cost lever at a kiosk, where forty questions repeat thousands of times a day. **Invalidated by the same events that invalidate the index** — a cached answer that outlives a price change has misled a guest on the venue’s behalf. **`scope_path` is part of the key**: a cache keyed on the question alone is a cross-venue leak wearing a performance hat
storage.cache:embedding: Content hash and model to a vector. **A tenant editing fifty of twenty thousand chunks re-embeds fifty.** Invalidation is trivial because the key changes when the content does
storage.cache:resolution: Scope and permission resolution, tenant configuration, price lists. **Read on every request and changed rarely** — `resolvePermissions` reads five tables on every authorised call
storage.cache:idempotency: Seen idempotency keys. **Every write carries one as of 17 August and nothing said where the record lived or how long it was kept** — a key store that forgets too early lets a replay through, which is the defect the key exists to prevent. Retention must exceed the longest offline window (ADR-0013) **Retention must exceed the longest offline window** — a scanner out for a weekend replays on Monday, and a key store that expired on Sunday lets every one of those writes through twice.
